note: The main banks: the three largest US banks by consolidated assets in the Federal Reserve's list of large commercial banks are JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America and Citibank. Chase's full personal range is written; Bank of America's and Citi's are not, and neither is Capital One's, tried in their place. Bank of America's terms and conditions page loads each card's disclosure from secure.bankofamerica.com, which answered with a captcha (not circumvented); Citi's and Capital One's card pages load their pricing by script from their application systems (Citi's page didn't finish loading when rendered), so no card's terms could be read from them on 2026-10-30. Chase: every personal card on its all-credit-cards page (read 2026-10-30), 32 of them, each from its own Pricing and Terms page (the costs accurate as of 9/22/2026, the Prime Rate 7.00% that day); the 11 business cards (Ink, Sapphire Reserve for Business, the United, Southwest, IHG and Hyatt business cards) aren't written. Each card's purchase APR is written as its range, the bank setting each holder's rate within it by creditworthiness; a 0% introductory purchase APR for its months where the card has one; the annual membership fee (the United Explorer's $0 first year written as its first year waived; the Sapphire Reserve's $195 for each authorized user isn't written); the cash advance APR and fee (the greater of a floor and a share of the advance); the foreign transaction fee (written as 0 where the box says None); the late payment and returned payment fees, each 'up to' a figure, written at that figure; and the penalty APR, 'up to' a figure, written at it. The due date is at least 21 days after each billing cycle closes and no interest is charged on purchases if the whole balance is paid by then; that is the least time the bank promises, not the most a purchase goes without interest, so no grace is written. Balance transfer APRs and fees, the Chase Pay Over Time fee (a plan the holder chooses) and the Military Lending Act terms aren't written; the boxes state no over-limit fee (None) and no limit rule; the minimum payment is in the agreements, below. The Amazon and Prime Visa cards' late and returned payment fees are up to $39 and their cash advance fee the greater of $5 or 4%. The earlier reading of the Freedom Unlimited (2026-10-29) is kept as a source; its figures hold. On 2026-10-30 two more issuers were added. Wells Fargo, among the four largest US banks in the same list: every personal card whose terms page its credit-cards page links (six; the One Key cards' terms load by script and aren't written; business cards aren't written), each from its terms page: the purchase APR range by creditworthiness, a 0% introductory APR for its months where the card has one, the annual fee, the cash advance APR and fee (the greater of $10 or 5%), the foreign transaction fee (None written as 0) and the late fee 'up to $40', written at $40; the due date at least 25 days after the billing period closes isn't a grace period and isn't written, nor are balance transfer terms or the $1 minimum interest charge. American Express (its own application terms pages answered 403, 'the online application is currently unavailable'): the Rates and Fees Table of each personal card agreement American Express National Bank filed with the CFPB's credit card agreement database for the second quarter of 2026 (as of 06/30/2026), 24 cards; the Blue from American Express and Morgan Stanley Credit Card agreements (as of 2021) and the Optima Card's are older products no longer marketed and aren't written. Each APR is the Prime Rate plus a margin; the Prime Rate is 7.00% (the Federal Reserve's H.15, bank prime loan, 22 to 28 October 2026), and each sum is written, a penalty APR above the agreements' ceiling ('Variable APRs will not exceed 29.99%') written at 29.99%. The charge cards (American Express Gold Card, American Express Green Card, Centurion Card, Platinum Card from American Express Exclusively for Charles Schwab, Goldman Sachs Platinum Card, Platinum Card from American Express exclusively for Morgan Stanley, Platinum Card) carry the Pay Over Time APR as their rate, the balance being due in full except what the holder's Pay Over Time feature carries. The cash advance fee is the greater of $10 or 5%; the foreign transaction fee 2.7% or None (written as 0); late and returned payment fees 'up to $40', written at $40 (the first is $29, as each agreement explains); the Centurion's $10,000 initiation fee written as its issue fee. Plan It fees, balance transfer terms and additional cards' fees aren't written. U.S. Bank's and Discover's (now a division of Capital One) card pages load their APRs by script, so their agreements in the CFPB database for the second quarter of 2026 were read instead. U.S. Bank's agreement for its Visa and Mastercard Classic, Gold and Platinum accounts (accurate as of 30 June 2026) gives one pricing table for them all, written as one card: purchases 16.99% to 28.49%, cash advances 29.49% to 30.49%, no penalty rate, no annual fee, a cash advance fee the greater of $10 or 5%, a foreign transaction fee 'up to 3%' written at 3, late and returned payment fees 'up to $41' written at 41; the per-product pages (Cash+, Altitude, Shield and others) aren't written separately. Discover's prime cardmember agreement and pricing schedule (terms for recent applicants as of 30 June 2026), written as the Discover Card: purchases 17.49% to 26.49%, cash advances 28.49%, no penalty APR or annual fee, cash advance fee the greater of $10 or 5%, the late fee 'none the first time, after that up to $41' written at 41, returned payment up to $30; the schedule names no foreign transaction fee, so none is written. Minimum payments (wave 5, read 30 October 2026, from the agreements each issuer filed with the CFPB's credit card agreement database for the second quarter of 2026). Chase: the larger of $40 (or the whole balance if less) or 1% of the new balance plus the interest and late fees billed, written as 1% with a $40 floor and the interest on top; every English personal cardmember agreement Chase filed (the agreements are numbered, not named, so each card can't be matched to its own) states it, except agreement COL00067, the Amazon cards', whose floor is $35, written for the Prime Visa and Amazon Visa. Wells Fargo: each card's own account agreement: the greater of 1% of the new balance plus the interest and the annual, late and rush-plastic fees billed, or $25, written as 1% with a $25 floor and the interest on top. American Express: the credit cards' agreements give the highest of the interest plus 1% of the new balance, 2% of the new balance, or $40, written as 1% with a $40 floor and the interest on top (the 2% arm, which is higher only in a month with little or no interest, isn't modelled); the charge cards' Pay Over Time minimum is the highest of $40, 2%, or 1% of the balance up to $20,000 (2%, 5% and 10% of the parts above $20,000, $35,000 and $50,000) plus the interest, written the same way, the tiers above $20,000 and the Pay In Full balance due in full each month not modelled. U.S. Bank: the greater of $40 or 1% of the new balance, with the interest and fees added, written as 1% with a $40 floor and the interest on top. Discover: the greater of $35, 2% of the new balance, or $20 plus the interest and late fees billed, written as 2% with a $35 floor; the third arm, higher whenever a month's interest is above about $15 and the balance's 2% less than $20 plus the interest, isn't in the form and isn't modelled. In every case, fees added on top of the share and amounts over the limit or past due aren't modelled.
